newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks dip in early morning trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks dip in early morning trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks dipped early Thursday morning on the back of weaknesss in bank issues and concerns that direct Sino-Taiwan shipping links may hurt the territory, but the long-term view remained confident, brokers said.

"The long-term bullish stance that many fund manager have taken is still intact, said James Robertson, vice president of Salomon Brothers. "If people are nervous about cross-straits shipping, they are about two years out of date,"
The Hang Seng Index was trading 60 points lower at 13,632 after 40 minutes of trade but off the morning's low of 13,593.49. Turnover was a healthy HK$1.57 million.
"Recent weakness in HSBC has brought the market down and put people in a profit-taking mood," said Pauline Cheung, chief dealer at South China Securities.
The banking giant, however, was unchanged at HK$178.50, while its subsidiary Hang Seng Bank lost HK$0.50 to HK$92.75. Medium-sized bank Dao Heng eased HK$1.60 to HK$39.00.
On Wednesday, Taiwan and China reached an understanding to let shipping firms apply to open routes between the two sides, raising prospects of direct shipping links after a long ban.
Since much of current cross-Straits trade passes through Hong Kong, brokers said the territory may lose some business.

Brokers cited container terminal operator Hutchison Whampoa as one of the companies to be affected by the cross straits development. Hutchison dipped HK$0.25 to HK$64.00 and parent Cheung Kong lost HK$0.50 to HK$75.00.
The property sector led the market down followed by the commercial and industrial sector. H shares also came in for profit-taking.
New World Development shed HK$0.95 to HK$49.80. Property analyst and director of Peregrine Securities Adrian Ngan said the stock looks fairly valued at current levels.
Great Eagle slipped HK$0.80 to HK$34.80.mong the hongs, Wharf dropped HK$0.50 to HK$37.70 and CITIC Pacific eased HK$0.40 to HK$38.80.
In the H share sector, profit taking pulled Guangdong Kelon down HK$0.10 to HK$5.85. Tsingtao Brewery also fell HK$0.10 to HK$3.15.
Trade in Hang Seng Index futures was quiet, with the January contract up 13 points to 13,633 on trade of only 3,087 contracts.
